text:
This looks like early 2012. Unemployment is 8.3%, which matches February 2012. The fed funds rate is about 0.13%, and the 10-year yield is 2.18%. Headline CPI is 2.89%, which matches February 2012, and core CPI is 2.17%.

US large-cap equity returned +22.6% over 6 months, and the 12-month return is +8.4%. The 6-month window runs from the lows around September 2011 to February or March 2012. The 3-month return of +12.1% fits the end of March 2012. The 1-month return of +2.7% fits March 2012 (the S&P 500 gained about 3%), and the 10-year yield was about 2.2% at the end of March. The 20y+ Treasury return of -3.3% for the month fits March as well, since yields rose then. The unemployment rate was 8.2% in March, but the figure published at the end of March would still be the February value of 8.3%. This points to March 2012.

Gold at -2.7% for the month fits March 2012 too.
